comparator.name: Applied Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: The formally adopted 2026-2027 appendix defines a 165-ECTS Applied Mathematics major and 15-ECTS minor. Year 1 is a compulsory 60-ECTS common Mathematics/Applied Mathematics foundation. The remaining 120 ECTS comprise 105 ECTS of major requirements and 15 ECTS of genuine minor space. First-year Project Applied Mathematics is used because it directly represents the named degree. For the two required project choices, Project Mathematical Modelling and Project Systems Theory are selected as the first two options in official order. Numerical Linear Algebra and Advanced Systems Theory are likewise the first two options in the required advanced-choice group. Statistical Modelling is the first Applied Mathematics elective not already used. These choices are fixed independently of UCR fit, and the open minor remains unpopulated. The official programme page and adopted appendix were rechecked on 2026-10-14; the settled curriculum and neutral choices remain unchanged. core: Applied mathematical modelling, numerical mathematics, systems and control, optimisation, proofs, calculus, linear algebra, probability and differential equations
Scientific programming, computational simulation, algorithms and data-based modelling
Translating real systems into tractable quantitative models and evaluating assumptions and solutions

Mathematical and computational models of living and biomedical systems
questions: How can mathematical, numerical and computational models describe, predict and optimise complex systems?
How can quantitative models be applied honestly to technological, physical and biological problems?

alternatives.label: Mathematical modelling, algorithms & autonomous systems
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by mathematics, programming, algorithms, data, optimisation, linear systems, machine learning and robotics, with a smaller sustainable-technology application strand. The label does not claim proof-based analysis, topology, functional analysis, partial differential equations or Applied Mathematics project formation.
alternatives.concept: Develop calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, linear systems, probability, programming, algorithms, optimisation, machine learning, robotics and autonomous decision methods, with sustainable-technology applications. This is the strongest quantitative related-fields response, not an Applied Mathematics degree.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and nine level-300 courses. Programming precedes algorithms and autonomous-system work; Mathematical Methods precedes dependent mathematics, robotics and neural networks; Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and Renewable System Design. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort term.

alternatives.label: Mathematical modelling, Earth systems & sustainable technology
alternatives.labelReason: Six Earth and environmental courses replace six specialist algorithmic courses, producing a natural-system, resource and sustainable-technology curriculum while keeping quantitative modelling central. The label does not imply Applied Mathematics, physics or engineering equivalence.
alternatives.concept: Combine mathematical and computational models with Earth-system science, geospatial and laboratory investigation, water–mineral interactions, resource recovery, climate mitigation and renewable-system assessment. This implements the target-linked mathematics-in-engineering-and-physics direction through available natural-system applications without claiming an Applied Mathematics curriculum.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and eight level-300 courses. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and all dependent resource and energy courses; Mathematical Methods precedes later mathematics, robotics and neural-network study. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort term.
alternatives.distinctness: Six courses, or 45 EC, differ in each direction. Optimisation, computer networks, algorithms, advanced algorithms, AI decision-making and reinforcement learning are replaced by Earth-system modelling, Dynamic Earth, soils and aquifers, environmental biogeochemistry, resource recovery and advanced resource research. These changes implement a natural physical-systems direction rather than threshold-filling substitutions.

alternatives.label: Quantitative bioscience, imaging & computational modelling
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum contains a sustained molecular, physiological, neurobiological, laboratory and disease-science core alongside mathematics, programming, imaging and data modelling. It does not claim mathematical biology, biophysics or Applied Mathematics equivalence.
alternatives.concept: Study living and human systems through molecular biology, physiology, neurobiology, laboratory work and disease mechanisms, combined with calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, signals, probability, programming, machine learning and image analysis. This implements the target-linked biological-modelling direction through related quantitative bioscience rather than a mathematical-biology or Applied Mathematics curriculum.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and seven level-300 courses. Life-science, biomedical and brain foundations precede dependent molecular, anatomical, physiological, disease and cognitive courses; Mathematical Methods precedes advanced quantitative work. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort term.
alternatives.distinctness: Against the autonomous-systems route, fourteen courses (105 EC) differ in each direction; against the Earth-and-energy route, thirteen courses (97.5 EC) differ in each direction. The third programme replaces most specialist algorithms, autonomy, Earth, resource and energy study with molecular, physiological, neurobiological, laboratory and disease science, as required by the medical-technology direction.

candidates.label: Engineering, physical systems and sustainable technology

selection.assessment: The historical judgment correctly identified the absent proof-based and advanced applied-mathematics spine but incorrectly treated full disciplinary equivalence as necessary. The first programme is the strongest feasible quantitative and computational systems response. The separately evidenced engineering/physical-systems and biological-modelling directions each support a coherent and materially different complete route, and all three pass the pairwise distinctness floor. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

blocks: Both develop programming and computational problem solving; UCR uses general Python programming rather than a mathematics-specific scientific-programming course.
Both develop formal logic and discrete mathematical structures; UCR applies them to decision-making and algorithm construction rather than reproducing Groningen's proof-based sets-and-numbers course.
Both establish calculus and equation-solving foundations; UCR also introduces matrices, eigenvalues, complex numbers and differential equations.
Both address optimisation; UCR focuses on search and constraint-satisfaction methods for AI rather than a full applied-mathematics optimisation course.
Both directly study systems of equations, vectors, matrices and linear spaces; Groningen continues to a second dedicated linear-algebra course.
Both study root-finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration, differential-equation methods, accuracy, stability and efficiency.
Both analyse linear systems through differential equations and state-space or related representations; UCR does not continue to Groningen's advanced systems-theory sequence.
Both use mathematical and algorithmic methods for computational problems; UCR emphasises algebraic algorithms and optimisation rather than the full Groningen computational-science component.
Both establish probability concepts and distributions; UCR combines probability with statistical inference and simulation.
Both develop statistical models; UCR teaches regression, classification and machine-learning methods rather than Groningen's dedicated Statistical Modelling elective.
Both extend calculus beyond the introductory level; UCR includes multivariable calculus, complex-valued functions and differential equations but not the target's full analysis sequence.
Both construct and evaluate models of complex systems; UCR does so specifically for interacting Earth systems rather than as a general applied-mathematics modelling course.
Both address professional and societal responsibility; UCR PPD is general formation and does not reproduce mathematics-specific ethical and professional analysis.

The comparator requires a 15-EC Applied Mathematics research project; UCR optional independent research is shown separately and does not supply disciplinary mathematics supervision or the target's proof and modelling preparation.

notes.text: The UCR programmes develop mathematical and computational modelling, algorithms and autonomous systems, Earth and sustainable-system analysis, and quantitative biomedical perspectives. They do not reproduce the target's cumulative proof-based analysis, topology, complex and functional analysis, ordinary and partial differential equations, advanced numerical and systems theory, staged modelling projects or Applied Mathematics research project.
